source.text: וַיְצַ֞ו אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־בֵּיתוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ מַלֵּ֞א אֶת־אַמְתְּחֹ֤ת הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֹ֔כֶל כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יוּכְל֖וּן שְׂאֵ֑ת וְשִׂ֥ים כֶּֽסֶף־אִ֖ישׁ בְּפִ֥י אַמְתַּחְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he commanded [the one] who [was] over his house, saying, fill the sacks of the men [with] food, as they are able to carry, and put [the] silver of each man in [the] mouth of his sack.

en.L: And he commanded the [man] who [was] over his house, saying, "Fill the men's sacks [with] food, as much as they can carry, and put each man's silver in the mouth of his sack.
en.B: Joseph gave orders to the man in charge of his household: "Load these men's sacks with all the food they are able to carry, and put every man's money back at the top of his sack.
en.R: Then Joseph gave orders to the servant who ran his house. He said, "Put as much food in the men's bags as they can carry. Put each man's money back inside his bag, at the top.

decisions.choice: silver: the payment for the grain
decisions.reason: Kesef is the metal silver, weighed out as payment; there were no coins yet. As in 42:25 and 43:21, each brother's payment is secretly put back in his sack.

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "silver"; Balanced and Readable say "money" because the silver here is the price paid for grain. The cup in verse 2 stays a silver cup at every level.

decisions.choice: at the top of his sack
alternatives: in the mouth of his sack
decisions.reason: The "mouth" of a sack is its opening; the money is laid just inside it.

source.text: וְאֶת־גְּבִיעִ֞י גְּבִ֣יעַ הַכֶּ֗סֶף תָּשִׂים֙ בְּפִי֙ אַמְתַּ֣חַת הַקָּטֹ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת כֶּ֣סֶף שִׁבְר֑וֹ וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כִּדְבַ֥ר יוֹסֵ֖ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And my cup, [the] cup of silver, you will put in [the] mouth of [the] sack of the youngest, and [the] silver of his grain. And he did according to [the] word of Joseph which he had spoken.

en.L: And my cup, the silver cup, you shall put in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, together with the silver for his grain." And he did as Joseph had told [him].
en.B: And put my cup, the silver one, in the top of the youngest one's sack, along with the money he paid for his grain." The steward carried out Joseph's instructions.
en.R: Put my silver cup in the top of the youngest brother's bag too, with the money he paid for his grain." The servant did what Joseph told him.

decisions.choice: cup: a goblet or bowl for drinking
decisions.reason: Gavia is a large drinking vessel, a goblet or bowl, also used for the bowls of the lampstand (Exodus 25:31-34). Here it is Joseph's own personal cup (verse 5).

source.text: הַבֹּ֖קֶר א֑וֹר וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים שֻׁלְּח֔וּ הֵ֖מָּה וַחֲמֹרֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: The morning was light, and the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.

en.L: The morning was light, and the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
en.B: At first light the men were sent off with their donkeys.
en.R: Early the next morning, as soon as it was light, the brothers were sent on their way with their donkeys.

source.text: הֵ֠ם יָֽצְא֣וּ אֶת־הָעִיר֮ לֹ֣א הִרְחִיקוּ֒ וְיוֹסֵ֤ף אָמַר֙ לַֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־בֵּית֔וֹ ק֥וּם רְדֹ֖ף אַחֲרֵ֣י הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְהִשַּׂגְתָּם֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם לָ֛מָּה שִׁלַּמְתֶּ֥ם רָעָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת טוֹבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: They went out of the city, not had they gone far, and Joseph said to [the one] who [was] over his house, arise, pursue after the men, and you will overtake them and you will say to them, why have you repaid evil for good?

en.L: They had gone out of the city [and] had not gone far, when Joseph said to the [man] who [was] over his house, "Get up, pursue the men, and when you overtake them, say to them, 'Why have you repaid evil for good?
en.B: They had left the city and were still close by when Joseph told his steward, "Go after those men at once. When you catch up with them, ask them, 'Why have you paid back good with evil?
en.R: They had not gone far from the city when Joseph said to his servant, "Hurry, go after those men! When you catch them, say to them, 'I was good to you. Why have you done something evil to me?

decisions.choice: why have you repaid evil for good?: the brothers' old guilt in a new form
decisions.reason: The charge echoes what the brothers once did to Joseph. He later says of their deed, "you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good" (50:20).

decisions.choice: I was good to you. Why have you done something evil to me?
alternatives: Why have you repaid evil for good?
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the idiom "repay evil for good" as two plain sentences.

source.text: הֲל֣וֹא זֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁתֶּ֤ה אֲדֹנִי֙ בּ֔וֹ וְה֕וּא נַחֵ֥שׁ יְנַחֵ֖שׁ בּ֑וֹ הֲרֵעֹתֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲשִׂיתֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] not this [that] which my lord drinks from it, and he indeed practices divination with it? You have done evil [in that] which you have done.

en.L: Is this not [the cup] from which my lord drinks, and with which he indeed practices divination? You have done wrong in doing this.'"
en.B: Is this not the cup my master drinks from, the one he uses to read omens? What you have done is wicked.'"
en.R: This is the cup my master drinks from. He also uses it to learn secret things. You have done a very wrong thing.'"

decisions.choice: he practices divination with it: reading signs in a cup
decisions.reason: In the ancient Near East some diviners poured water or oil into a bowl and read signs in the patterns. The steward speaks as Joseph's household would; the text does not say Joseph actually did this, and he is playing a part. Israel's law later forbade divination (Leviticus 19:26; Deuteronomy 18:10).

decisions.choice: the cup
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "this"; the cup is meant. Literal brackets the word.

source.text: וַֽיַּשִּׂגֵ֑ם וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he overtook them and spoke to them these words.

en.L: And he overtook them and spoke these words to them.
en.B: When he caught up with them, he repeated those words to them.
en.R: The servant caught up with the brothers and said to them what Joseph had told him to say.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו לָ֚מָּה יְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲדֹנִ֔י כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה חָלִ֨ילָה֙ לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ מֵעֲשׂ֖וֹת כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, why does my lord speak according to these words? Far be it for your servants from doing according to this thing.

en.L: And they said to him, "Why does my lord speak words like these? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing!
en.B: "Why would my lord say such things?" they answered. "Your servants would never do anything of the kind!
en.R: They answered, "Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!

decisions.choice: far be it: an oath-like denial
decisions.reason: Chalilah expresses strong rejection, "that is unthinkable" (as in 18:25).

decisions.choice: your servants: a polite way of saying "we"
decisions.reason: Speaking of oneself as "your servant" was a common courtesy (18:3).

source.text: הֵ֣ן כֶּ֗סֶף אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָצָ֨אנוּ֙ בְּפִ֣י אַמְתְּחֹתֵ֔ינוּ הֱשִׁיבֹ֥נוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וְאֵ֗יךְ נִגְנֹב֙ מִבֵּ֣ית אֲדֹנֶ֔יךָ כֶּ֖סֶף א֥וֹ זָהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Here, [the] silver which we found in [the] mouth of our sacks we brought back to you from [the] land of Canaan; and how would we steal from [the] house of your master silver or gold?

en.L: Look, the silver that we found in the mouth of our sacks we brought back to you from the land of Canaan. How then would we steal silver or gold from your master's house?
en.B: Remember, we brought back to you from Canaan the money we found in the tops of our sacks. Why would we then steal silver or gold from your master's house?
en.R: We even brought back from Canaan the money we found in our bags. So why would we steal silver or gold from your master's house?

decisions.choice: the silver ... we brought back: proof of their honesty
decisions.reason: The brothers point to 43:21-22: they returned the money found in their sacks the first time, so why would they now steal?

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִמָּצֵ֥א אִתּ֛וֹ מֵעֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וָמֵ֑ת וְגַם־אֲנַ֕חְנוּ נִֽהְיֶ֥ה לַֽאדֹנִ֖י לַעֲבָדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: [Anyone] with whom it is found of your servants, he shall die; and also we, we will become to my lord slaves.

en.L: Whoever of your servants [it] is found with, let him die, and we also will become my lord's slaves."
en.B: If any one of us is found to have it, he must die, and the rest of us will become your slaves, my lord."
en.R: If you find the cup with any of us, that man must die. And all the rest of us will become your slaves."

decisions.choice: he shall die: a rash oath
decisions.reason: Like Jacob in 31:32, the brothers pronounce a death sentence on whoever has the stolen object, sure that none of them does.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" at every level: becoming slaves is the penalty offered, set against going free (verse 10), so the style guide keeps the word. The polite "your servants" in Literal is a different use.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר גַּם־עַתָּ֥ה כְדִבְרֵיכֶ֖ם כֶּן־ה֑וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִמָּצֵ֤א אִתּוֹ֙ יִהְיֶה־לִּ֣י עָ֔בֶד וְאַתֶּ֖ם תִּהְי֥וּ נְקִיִּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, also now, according to your words, so it [will be]: [the one] with whom it is found will be to me a slave, and you will be innocent.

en.L: And he said, "Now then, let it be as you say: the one with whom it is found shall be my slave, and the rest of you shall be innocent."
en.B: "Very well," he replied, "it will be as you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave; the rest of you will go free of blame."
en.R: The servant said, "All right, we will do what you say. But only the man who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you will be free."

decisions.choice: a lighter penalty than the brothers proposed
decisions.reason: The steward accepts their words but changes the terms: not death and slavery for all, only slavery for the guilty man. This sets up the test that follows: will the brothers abandon Benjamin?

decisions.choice: innocent: free of guilt and obligation
decisions.reason: Naqi means clear, released from guilt or from a penalty (24:41).

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level: the guilty man becomes a slave while the rest go free (m1), so the style guide keeps the word.

source.text: וַֽיְמַהֲר֗וּ וַיּוֹרִ֛דוּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־אַמְתַּחְתּ֖וֹ אָ֑רְצָה וַֽיִּפְתְּח֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ אַמְתַּחְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they hurried and brought down each man his sack to the ground, and they opened each man his sack.

en.L: Then each man quickly lowered his sack to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
en.B: Each of them quickly lowered his sack to the ground and opened it.
en.R: Each brother quickly put his bag down on the ground and opened it.

source.text: וַיְחַפֵּ֕שׂ בַּגָּד֣וֹל הֵחֵ֔ל וּבַקָּטֹ֖ן כִּלָּ֑ה וַיִּמָּצֵא֙ הַגָּבִ֔יעַ בְּאַמְתַּ֖חַת בִּנְיָמִֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he searched; with the oldest he began and with the youngest he finished; and was found the cup in [the] sack of Benjamin.

en.L: And he searched, beginning with the oldest and finishing with the youngest, and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
en.B: The steward searched, starting with the eldest and ending with the youngest, and the cup turned up in Benjamin's sack.
en.R: The servant looked through the bags. He started with the oldest brother's bag and ended with the youngest. The cup was in Benjamin's bag.

decisions.choice: from the oldest to the youngest: a search that builds suspense
decisions.reason: The search follows birth order, as the seating at Joseph's table had (43:33), so the cup is found last, in Benjamin's sack.

source.text: וַֽיִּקְרְע֖וּ שִׂמְלֹתָ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲמֹס֙ אִ֣ישׁ עַל־חֲמֹר֔וֹ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ הָעִֽירָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they tore their clothes, and loaded each man on his donkey and they returned to the city.

en.L: And they tore their clothes, and each man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city.
en.B: At this they tore their clothes. Then each of them loaded his donkey again, and they went back to the city.
en.R: The brothers were so upset that they tore their clothes. They loaded their donkeys again and went back to the city.

decisions.choice: they tore their clothes: a sign of grief and horror
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes showed anguish. Reuben and Jacob had done the same over Joseph (37:29, 34); now all the brothers do it over Benjamin, and they do not leave him to his fate.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א יְהוּדָ֤ה וְאֶחָיו֙ בֵּ֣יתָה יוֹסֵ֔ף וְה֖וּא עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ שָׁ֑ם וַיִּפְּל֥וּ לְפָנָ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Judah and his brothers to [the] house of Joseph, and he [was] still there; and they fell before him to the ground.

en.L: And Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house, and he was still there; and they fell before him to the ground.
en.B: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house while he was still there, and they threw themselves down on the ground before him.
en.R: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house. Joseph was still there, and they bowed down to the ground in front of him.

decisions.choice: Judah and his brothers: Judah now leads
decisions.reason: Judah, who pledged himself for Benjamin (43:8-9), is named first and speaks for all of them. The brothers bowing to the ground fulfill Joseph's dreams once more (37:7).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ יוֹסֵ֔ף מָֽה־הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֑ם הֲל֣וֹא יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם כִּֽי־נַחֵ֧שׁ יְנַחֵ֛שׁ אִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּמֹֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Joseph, what [is] this deed which you have done? Did you not know that indeed practices divination a man who [is] like me?

en.L: And Joseph said to them, "What is this deed that you have done? Did you not know that a man like me can indeed practice divination?"
en.B: "What have you done?" Joseph demanded. "Did you not realize that a man in my position can find things out by divination?"
en.R: Joseph asked them, "Why did you do this? Did you not know that a man like me can find out secret things?"

decisions.choice: a man like me can practice divination: Joseph keeps up his disguise
decisions.reason: Joseph speaks as an Egyptian official would be expected to. The narrator never says he used the cup this way; his knowledge of their deed comes from his own plan.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָ֗ה מַה־נֹּאמַר֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י מַה־נְּדַבֵּ֖ר וּמַה־נִּצְטַדָּ֑ק הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים מָצָא֙ אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ הִנֶּנּ֤וּ עֲבָדִים֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י גַּם־אֲנַ֕חְנוּ גַּ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־נִמְצָ֥א הַגָּבִ֖יעַ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Judah, what will we say to my lord? What will we speak, and how will we justify ourselves? God has found [the] guilt of your servants. Here we [are] slaves to my lord, both we and [the one] in whose hand the cup was found.

en.L: And Judah said, "What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak? Or how can we clear ourselves? God has found out the guilt of your servants. Here we are, my lord's slaves, both we and the one in whose hand the cup was found."
en.B: "My lord, what can we say?" Judah answered. "What words do we have? How could we prove we are innocent? God has exposed your servants' guilt. We are your slaves now, my lord, all of us, not just the one who had the cup."
en.R: Judah said, "Sir, what can we say? How can we show that we did nothing wrong? God has shown that we are guilty. So now all of us will be your slaves, not only the one who had the cup."

decisions.choice: God has found out the guilt of your servants: perhaps their old sin
decisions.reason: Judah does not admit stealing the cup; he says God has uncovered their guilt. The word avon is guilt for wrongdoing, and Judah may be thinking of what they did to Joseph years before (42:21-22).

decisions.choice: justify ourselves: show ourselves to be in the right
decisions.reason: The verb is from the root of tsaddiq, "righteous": how can we prove we are in the right?

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" at every level for the brothers' offer to become slaves as the penalty (verses 9-10), so the style guide keeps the word; the polite "your servants" earlier in the verse stays distinct.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר חָלִ֣ילָה לִּ֔י מֵעֲשׂ֖וֹת זֹ֑את הָאִ֡ישׁ אֲשֶׁר֩ נִמְצָ֨א הַגָּבִ֜יעַ בְּיָד֗וֹ ה֚וּא יִהְיֶה־לִּ֣י עָ֔בֶד וְאַתֶּ֕ם עֲל֥וּ לְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶל־אֲבִיכֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he said, far be it to me from doing this; the man in whose hand the cup was found, he will be my slave; and you, go up in peace to your father.

en.L: But he said, "Far be it from me to do this! The man in whose hand the cup was found, he shall be my slave. As for you, go up in peace to your father."
en.B: But Joseph answered, "I would never do such a thing! Only the one who had the cup will be my slave. The rest of you may return safely to your father."
en.R: But Joseph said, "No, I will not do that. Only the man who had my cup will be my slave. The rest of you can go home safely to your father."

decisions.choice: go up in peace to your father: the test
decisions.reason: Joseph offers the brothers the same choice they once made: to go home free and leave Rachel's son behind as a slave in Egypt (37:28). What they do now shows whether they have changed.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level: one man stays as a slave and the rest go home free (m1), so the style guide keeps the word.

source.text: וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ אֵלָ֜יו יְהוּדָ֗ה וַיֹּאמֶר֮ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִי֒ יְדַבֶּר־נָ֨א עַבְדְּךָ֤ דָבָר֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י וְאַל־יִ֥חַר אַפְּךָ֖ בְּעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י כָמ֖וֹךָ כְּפַרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And drew near to him Judah and said, pardon, my lord, let speak, please, your servant a word in [the] ears of my lord, and let not burn your anger against your servant, for like you [are] like Pharaoh.

en.L: Then Judah approached him and said, "Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord's ears, and do not let your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh himself.
en.B: Then Judah stepped up to him and said, "Forgive me, my lord, but let your servant say something to you in private, and please do not be angry with your servant, for you are as great as Pharaoh.
en.R: Then Judah went up to Joseph and said, "Please, sir, let me say something to you. Do not be angry with me. You have as much power as Pharaoh himself.

decisions.choice: bi: "please, pardon", a humble opening to a request
decisions.reason: Bi is a polite particle used when asking a superior for a hearing.

decisions.choice: in my lord's ears: speak directly to him
decisions.reason: To speak "in someone's ears" is to speak so that he hears in person. Judah asks for a personal hearing.

decisions.choice: you are like Pharaoh: your word is as final as the king's
decisions.reason: Judah acknowledges Joseph's power: his decision is as binding as Pharaoh's. Judah's speech that follows (verses 18-34) is the longest in Genesis.

source.text: אֲדֹנִ֣י שָׁאַ֔ל אֶת־עֲבָדָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר הֲיֵשׁ־לָכֶ֥ם אָ֖ב אוֹ־אָֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: My lord asked his servants, saying, is there to you a father or a brother?

en.L: My lord asked his servants, saying, 'Do you have a father or a brother?'
en.B: My lord asked your servants whether we had a father or another brother.
en.R: Sir, you asked us, 'Do you have a father or a brother?'

decisions.choice: my lord asked his servants: polite third person
decisions.reason: Judah addresses Joseph as "my lord" and speaks of himself and his brothers as "his servants", the courteous form of speech before a ruler.

source.text: וַנֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֔י יֶשׁ־לָ֨נוּ֙ אָ֣ב זָקֵ֔ן וְיֶ֥לֶד זְקֻנִ֖ים קָטָ֑ן וְאָחִ֨יו מֵ֜ת וַיִּוָּתֵ֨ר ה֧וּא לְבַדּ֛וֹ לְאִמּ֖וֹ וְאָבִ֥יו אֲהֵבֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And we said to my lord, there is to us a father, old, and a child of old age, young; and his brother died, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.

en.L: And we said to my lord, 'We have a father, an old man, and a young son of his old age. His brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.'
en.B: We answered, 'We have an elderly father, and there is a young son born to him in his old age. The boy's brother is dead; he is the only one of his mother's sons still living, and his father loves him dearly.'
en.R: We told you, 'We have a father who is old. He also has a young son who was born when he was old. The boy's brother is dead, so he is the only son of his mother left. His father loves him very much.'

decisions.choice: a child of old age: born when his father was old
decisions.reason: The same phrase described Joseph in 37:3. Benjamin is now the favored son of Rachel.

decisions.choice: his brother is dead: Judah believes Joseph dead, speaking to Joseph
decisions.reason: Judah says this to the brother he thinks is dead. The irony is strong for the reader.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ הוֹרִדֻ֖הוּ אֵלָ֑י וְאָשִׂ֥ימָה עֵינִ֖י עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And you said to your servants, bring him down to me, that I may set my eye on him.

en.L: Then you said to your servants, 'Bring him down to me, so that I may set my eyes on him.'
en.B: Then you told your servants, 'Bring him down here so I can see him for myself.'
en.R: Then you said to us, 'Bring him here to me. I want to see him.'

decisions.choice: set my eye on him: see him, perhaps also look after him
decisions.reason: To set one's eye on someone can mean simply to see him, or to watch over him kindly (Jeremiah 39:12).

source.text: וַנֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֔י לֹא־יוּכַ֥ל הַנַּ֖עַר לַעֲזֹ֣ב אֶת־אָבִ֑יו וְעָזַ֥ב אֶת־אָבִ֖יו וָמֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And we said to my lord, not is able the young man to leave his father; and [if] he leaves his father, he will die.

en.L: And we said to my lord, 'The boy cannot leave his father; if he leaves his father, [his father] will die.'
en.B: We told my lord, 'The boy cannot leave his father. If he did, his father would die.'
en.R: We told you, 'The boy cannot leave his father. If he does, his father will die.'

decisions.choice: he will die: most likely the father
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he will die". It most likely means Jacob, who would die of grief (verses 29-31), though it could be read of the boy.

decisions.choice: his father will die
decisions.reason: The subject is supplied to show the reading taken, which matches verses 29-31.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ אִם־לֹ֥א יֵרֵ֛ד אֲחִיכֶ֥ם הַקָּטֹ֖ן אִתְּכֶ֑ם לֹ֥א תֹסִפ֖וּן לִרְא֥וֹת פָּנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And you said to your servants, if not comes down your youngest brother with you, not will you again see my face.

en.L: But you said to your servants, 'Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall not see my face again.'
en.B: But you told your servants, 'If your youngest brother does not come down with you, you will not be allowed to see me again.'
en.R: But you said to us, 'If your youngest brother does not come with you, you will never see me again.'

decisions.choice: see my face: be admitted to my presence
decisions.reason: To see a ruler's face is to come before him. Without Benjamin they could not even ask to buy grain (43:3, 5).

source.text: וַיְהִי֙ כִּ֣י עָלִ֔ינוּ אֶֽל־עַבְדְּךָ֖ אָבִ֑י וַנַּ֨גֶּד־ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when we went up to your servant my father, and we told him [the] words of my lord.

en.L: So it was, when we went up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
en.B: When we returned to your servant, my father, we reported to him everything my lord had said.
en.R: So when we went home to our father, we told him what you had said.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָבִ֑ינוּ שֻׁ֖בוּ שִׁבְרוּ־לָ֥נוּ מְעַט־אֹֽכֶל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said our father, go back, buy for us a little food.

en.L: And our father said, 'Go back, buy us a little food.'
en.B: Later our father told us, 'Go back and buy us a little more food.'
en.R: Later our father said, 'Go back to Egypt and buy us a little food.'

source.text: וַנֹּ֕אמֶר לֹ֥א נוּכַ֖ל לָרֶ֑דֶת אִם־יֵשׁ֩ אָחִ֨ינוּ הַקָּטֹ֤ן אִתָּ֨נוּ֙ וְיָרַ֔דְנוּ כִּי־לֹ֣א נוּכַ֗ל לִרְאוֹת֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָאִ֔ישׁ וְאָחִ֥ינוּ הַקָּטֹ֖ן אֵינֶ֥נּוּ אִתָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And we said, not are we able to go down; if there is our youngest brother with us, then we will go down; for not are we able to see [the] face of the man and our youngest brother not with us.

en.L: But we said, 'We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down; for we cannot see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us.'
en.B: But we said, 'We cannot go down there. We will go only if our youngest brother goes with us. Unless he is with us, the man will not see us.'
en.R: But we told him, 'We cannot go unless our youngest brother goes with us. The man will not let us see him if our youngest brother is not with us.'

source.text: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר עַבְדְּךָ֥ אָבִ֖י אֵלֵ֑ינוּ אַתֶּ֣ם יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם כִּ֥י שְׁנַ֖יִם יָֽלְדָה־לִּ֥י אִשְׁתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said your servant my father to us, you know that two my wife bore to me.

en.L: Then your servant my father said to us, 'You know that my wife bore me two [sons].
en.B: Your servant my father replied, 'You know that my wife gave me two sons.
en.R: Then our father said to us, 'You know that my wife Rachel gave me two sons.

decisions.choice: my wife: Rachel, as if she were his only wife
decisions.reason: Jacob speaks of Rachel simply as "my wife", as though Leah, the mother of Judah and most of the brothers standing there, did not count. Judah repeats the hurtful words without resentment.

decisions.choice: two sons
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "two"; sons are meant. Readable also names Rachel, which the context makes plain.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֤א הָֽאֶחָד֙ מֵֽאִתִּ֔י וָאֹמַ֕ר אַ֖ךְ טָרֹ֣ף טֹרָ֑ף וְלֹ֥א רְאִיתִ֖יו עַד־הֵֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out the one from with me, and I said, surely torn, he has been torn to pieces; and not have I seen him until now.

en.L: And the one went out from me, and I said, "Surely he has been torn to pieces," and I have not seen him since.
en.B: One of them left me, and I said, "He must have been torn apart by a wild animal." And I have never seen him again.
en.R: One of them went away from me. I thought, "A wild animal must have torn him to pieces." I have not seen him since then.

decisions.choice: torn to pieces: Jacob's words in 37:33
decisions.reason: Jacob repeats what he said when shown Joseph's bloodied robe. The doubled verb stresses certainty: "he must surely have been torn".

source.text: וּלְקַחְתֶּ֧ם גַּם־אֶת־זֶ֛ה מֵעִ֥ם פָּנַ֖י וְקָרָ֣הוּ אָס֑וֹן וְהֽוֹרַדְתֶּ֧ם אֶת־שֵׂיבָתִ֛י בְּרָעָ֖ה שְׁאֹֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [if] you take also this [one] from my presence and harm happens to him, then you will bring down my gray hair in calamity to Sheol.

en.L: If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, you will bring down my gray hair in evil to Sheol.'
en.B: If you take this one from me too, and something happens to him, you will send this gray head of mine down to the grave in misery.'
en.R: If you take this son from me too, and something bad happens to him, I will die of sorrow. You will send me, an old man, to my grave.'

decisions.choice: bring down my gray hair: cause an old man's death
decisions.reason: Gray hair stands for old age; to bring it down to Sheol is to bring an old man to his death (42:38).

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the Hebrew name for the realm of the dead, pictured as below the earth, where all go at death (37:35).

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew name Sheol; Balanced and Readable say "the grave", what the phrase means here.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה כְּבֹאִי֙ אֶל־עַבְדְּךָ֣ אָבִ֔י וְהַנַּ֖עַר אֵינֶ֣נּוּ אִתָּ֑נוּ וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹ קְשׁוּרָ֥ה בְנַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, when I come to your servant my father and the lad not with us, and his life [is] bound up with his life,

en.L: Now therefore, when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us, since his life is bound up with the boy's life,
en.B: So now, if I go back to your servant my father without the boy, since his life and the boy's life are tied together,
en.R: So now, think what will happen if I go back to my father without the boy. My father's life is tied up with the boy's life.

decisions.choice: his life is bound up with his life: the father lives for the boy
decisions.reason: Nefesh here is a person's life or self. Jacob's life is knotted to Benjamin's; to lose one is to lose the other (1 Samuel 18:1 uses the same picture for Jonathan and David).

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּרְאוֹת֛וֹ כִּי־אֵ֥ין הַנַּ֖עַר וָמֵ֑ת וְהוֹרִ֨ידוּ עֲבָדֶ֜יךָ אֶת־שֵׂיבַ֨ת עַבְדְּךָ֥ אָבִ֛ינוּ בְּיָג֖וֹן שְׁאֹֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: and it will be, when he sees that not [is] the lad, then he will die; and will bring down your servants [the] gray hair of your servant our father in sorrow to Sheol.

en.L: then when he sees that the boy is not [with us], he will die; and your servants will bring down the gray hair of your servant our father in sorrow to Sheol.
en.B: as soon as he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die. Your servants will have sent our father, your servant, to the grave, gray-haired and grieving.
en.R: When he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die. We will be the ones who sent our old father to his grave in sorrow.

decisions.choice: your servants will bring down: Judah takes the blame on the brothers
decisions.reason: Judah does not say the boy's loss would kill Jacob; he says the brothers would be the cause.

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: As in verse 29.

source.text: כִּ֤י עַבְדְּךָ֙ עָרַ֣ב אֶת־הַנַּ֔עַר מֵעִ֥ם אָבִ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־לֹ֤א אֲבִיאֶ֨נּוּ֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְחָטָ֥אתִי לְאָבִ֖י כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For your servant became surety for the lad from my father, saying, if not I bring him to you, then I will bear blame to my father all the days.

en.L: For your servant became surety for the boy to my father, saying, 'If I do not bring him back to you, then I shall bear the blame before my father all my life.'
en.B: Your servant guaranteed the boy's safety to my father. I told him, 'If I do not bring him back to you, I will be guilty before you, Father, all my life.'
en.R: I promised my father that I would keep the boy safe. I said, 'If I do not bring him back to you, you can blame me for the rest of my life.'

decisions.choice: became surety: pledged himself as guarantee
decisions.reason: Arav means to stand as a pledge for another, to answer with oneself for his safety (43:9).

decisions.choice: I will bear blame: literally "I will have sinned against my father"
decisions.reason: Chata, "to sin", here means to stand guilty and answerable before his father for the rest of his life.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה יֵֽשֶׁב־נָ֤א עַבְדְּךָ֙ תַּ֣חַת הַנַּ֔עַר עֶ֖בֶד לַֽאדֹנִ֑י וְהַנַּ֖עַר יַ֥עַל עִם־אֶחָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, let remain, please, your servant instead of the lad, a slave to my lord; and the lad, let him go up with his brothers.

en.L: So now, please let your servant remain in place of the boy as my lord's slave, and let the boy go up with his brothers.
en.B: Now then, please let me, your servant, stay here as my lord's slave instead of the boy, and let the boy go home with his brothers.
en.R: So please, let me stay here and be your slave in place of the boy. Let the boy go home with his brothers.

decisions.choice: in place of the boy: Judah offers himself
decisions.reason: The brother who once proposed selling Joseph into slavery (37:26-27) now offers to become a slave so that Rachel's other son may go free. This is the turning point of the Joseph story.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level: Judah offers to stay as a slave so that the boy may go free (m1), so the style guide keeps the word; "your servant" is his polite way of speaking of himself.

source.text: כִּי־אֵיךְ֙ אֶֽעֱלֶ֣ה אֶל־אָבִ֔י וְהַנַּ֖עַר אֵינֶ֣נּוּ אִתִּ֑י פֶּ֚ן אֶרְאֶ֣ה בָרָ֔ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִמְצָ֖א אֶת־אָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For how will I go up to my father and the lad not with me? Lest I look on the evil which will find my father.

en.L: For how can I go up to my father if the boy is not with me? I could not bear to see the evil that would come upon my father."
en.B: How could I go back to my father without the boy? I cannot bear to watch the misery it would bring him."
en.R: How can I go back to my father without the boy? I could not stand to see how much it would hurt him."

decisions.choice: lest I look on: I could not bear to see
decisions.reason: Pen, "lest", expresses Judah's dread: may I not have to watch my father's suffering.
